dossier.architecture: Tilting carbon-fiber elevator, roller gripper, separate wide cube intake and custom swerve.

subsystems.drivetrain: Custom lightweight swerve; impact compliance moved from wheel suspension to the mounting structure.
subsystems.intake: Wide belt collector for cubes; cones use the upper gripper.
subsystems.transfer: Cube intake presents pieces to powered gripper; escape space avoids trapping an extra piece.
subsystems.scoring: Carbon-fiber elevator tilts via sector gear to extend effective reach.
subsystems.endgame: Gyro-based station balance under development in the early-event interview.
subsystems.controls: Piece sensing, preset motion and autonomous cone/cube programs.

versions: Gripper evolved from gripping forks/material experiments to rollers. End-effector drive gears broke and were replaced by belts. Later CAD/code release documents the season robot.
dossier.analysis: Familiar fabrication methods can justify an elevator choice. The complete lesson includes stiffness, weight, retention and replacement of a failing transmission, rather than just the carbon-fiber material.
limits: Interview configuration and reported revisions are documented; full season chronology remains to be audited against the linked releases.

context_documents.title: 2023-2767 · A familiar carbon elevator reduces development uncertainty, not every failure mode
context_documents.body:
# 2023-2767: A familiar carbon elevator reduces development uncertainty, not every failure mode

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A wide cube collector feeds the upper gripper while cones use direct acquisition. A carbon elevator tilts on a sector mechanism; an escape region avoids trapping a second piece.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly cites prior carbon-elevator experience, limited build time and a desire for reliable fast scoring. Low mass addresses concern about crossing the charge station with a tall structure.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Mechanism familiarity is a legitimate resource constraint. Tilting extends effective reach but couples scoring geometry to support-polygon and drivetrain pitch. An extra-piece escape path must preserve control of the intended piece and the season’s possession rules.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test charge-station pitch with the mechanism safely stowed, tilt stiffness and rejection of an unintended extra piece.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/ngHZf3pnI14](https://youtu.be/ngHZf3pnI14)

source_reviews.title: 2767 Stryke Force CAD/Code Release 2023
source_reviews.review_basis: Read release and mechanism, revision and health-check answers.
source_reviews.facts: The carbon lift pivots on printed sectors, carries a powered elbow, and sits on chromoly and custom swerve. The team identifies specific changes between St. Joe and Worlds.
source_reviews.limitations: The release includes model links. This review uses the written explanations. A linked older account is described by the team as out of date.

source_reviews.title: Stryke Force Charged Up robot code
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the cube intake and floor cone branches and hand/intake implementations in the public checkout.
source_reviews.facts: Cube detection at the hand triggers a grab and intake retract. The cone branch uses a floor sweep and direct grab. The two branches coordinate different mechanisms.
source_reviews.limitations: The active control path is evidence for this snapshot. Commented steps and unused routines cannot establish match execution.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Stryke Force combined a tilting carbon-fiber elevator with an articulated carriage-mounted arm and hand. The drivetrain and arm have separate responsibilities for field pose and piece pose. For a cube, a chassis-mounted intake extends and presents the piece to the hand, whose state machine gates the transfer. For a cone, the arm and hand provide a direct floor acquisition path. The team reported driver initiation of automated mechanism sequences, with manual controls available for recovery.
source_review.piece_flow: In the reviewed floor-cube routine, intake travel reaches a sequencing threshold before the arm approaches its intake-stage pose. The collector starts running and the hand opens and spins its own roller. A cube indication at the hand commands a grab and collector retract to the pickup position. The routine waits on the hand, with an autonomous bypass of that wait, then uses a short timed phase before switching the hand roller to hold and stowing. The cone floor routine brings the hand to a floor pose, opens it, moves the arm through a sweep, closes at the sweep pose and stows when the hand move finishes. The two inputs therefore converge at the same hand for travel and placement.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The shoulder tilts the lift on printed sectors, the carriage moves along the carbon structure and the carriage elbow changes hand presentation. This distributes reach across three serial axes. The release also identifies left-right shoulder twist. As an engineering inference, a staged move prevents the elbow or hand from crossing the cube collector while it is still occupying the transfer envelope. The same serial chain magnifies any lost motion upstream into placement error at the hand.

subsystems.name: Carbon elevator and tilt
subsystems.construction: Single-stage carbon-fiber elevator, two carriage motors and printed Onyx pivot sectors. A carriage-mounted arm is driven by an Onyx gearbox.
subsystems.operation: Sector travel changes lift angle. Carriage travel and elbow angle change the hand's height and reach relative to the grid.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team reports enlarging the curved rack and improving elbow durability between St. Joe and Worlds. It describes iterating backlash when needed for smooth gear operation.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A tilted lift converts some travel to horizontal reach. Measure tooth engagement at both extremes with a loaded hand, where sector backlash and carriage deflection combine.
subsystems.interfaces: Tilt load enters the chromoly chassis. The carriage carries the elbow gearbox, hand and moving electrical services.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect sector tooth contact, printed gearbox fit and carbon-to-fitting joints. Compare open-loop current and speed after repairs.
subsystems.unknowns: Carriage rigging, bonded joint strength, tilt limits and actual load margins.

subsystems.name: Ground cube collector and hand
subsystems.construction: Motorized collector travel uses a Talon SRX with a profiled setpoint. The collector roller uses a Falcon controller. The hand has separately controlled jaw and roller motors. The team identifies bevel gears in the claw.
subsystems.operation: The collector stages a cube for the open hand. The hand uses a limit-input piece indication to advance to the grab, retract and hold sequence. The floor cone uses a dedicated hand posture and arm sweep.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team describes mechanism sequencing with driver initiation and a manual fallback. It reports enlarging the claw bevel gears for Worlds.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The pickup window requires matching roller directions, hand opening and collector pose. Time the transfer with worn cubes, including a sensor transition before the piece is fully seated.
subsystems.interfaces: The frame-mounted collector meets the moving hand at a defined arm pose. Piece confirmation ties jaw command and collector retract together.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check beam-break inputs and sensor zero after an impact. Try a partial cube insertion and verify the manual controls can clear it without driving an axis into another.
subsystems.unknowns: Collector width, exact roller contact geometry and quantitative transfer tolerance.

subsystems.name: Drivetrain and health checks
subsystems.construction: Chromoly frame and custom swerve with extensive printed Onyx parts. The team reports adding a 20 lb plate below the belly pan.
subsystems.operation: Drive input is limited during pickup and placement. AprilTag vision supports positioning and an open-loop health-check logs axis speed and current.
subsystems.team_rationale: Ballast was added for stability. The team uses current and speed comparisons to flag friction before closed-loop performance degrades.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Track comparable battery voltage and test load when comparing current traces, so voltage sag does not masquerade as gearbox friction.
subsystems.interfaces: The frame supports lift pivot loads. Camera placement on the elevator can change the view as the structure moves.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Compare drive azimuth velocity and current against the baseline after repairs. Check camera alignment after upper-structure impacts.
subsystems.unknowns: Module hardware loads, pose-dependent vision calibration and measured ramp behavior.

revisions: From St. Joe to Worlds, the team reports a taller sector rack, elbow gearbox durability revisions, a camera at the top of the elevator for autonomous AprilTag viewing and larger claw bevel gears. The team also reports adding underbody ballast after an initial weight around 100 lb.
transferable_principles: Use explicit transfer poses with piece confirmation at the receiving mechanism. Record open-loop current and velocity together to track binding that closed-loop control can hide.
disconfirming_conditions: A shared hand transfer loses cycle time if collector and arm tolerances require repeated grabs. A tilting lift loses reach advantages if slope and acceleration margins force conservative motion.
remaining_gaps: Event-by-event component fit, collector escape geometry, cycle-time distributions, and endurance of the printed sectors and carbon joints.

recommended_images.subject: Candidate team release illustrations for the carriage motors, composite joints and diagnostic current/velocity plots. Verify image attribution and configuration before reuse.
